root_cause.text: xe_exec_queue_create_ioctl() in the DRM/Xe exec queue subsystem had incorrect error-unwind ordering that freed an exec_queue without removing it from all owning lists (the VM compute exec queue list and hw_engine_group list), leaving stale references and causing dangling-pointer/use-after-free conditions.
root_cause.evidence: The patch changes the xe_hw_engine_group_add_exec_queue() failure path from `goto put_exec_queue` to `goto kill_exec_queue` so `xe_exec_queue_kill()` runs and removes the queue from the VM compute list, and adds a new `del_hw_engine_group` label before `kill_exec_queue` to call `xe_hw_engine_group_del_exec_queue()` when `xa_alloc()` fails after the queue was added to the hw engine group.

intent_record.intent_summary: Use the full exec queue teardown path when hardware engine group registration fails during exec queue creation.
intent_record.what: The error-handling branch after xe_hw_engine_group_add_exec_queue(q->hwe->hw_engine_group, q) was changed from jumping to the put_exec_queue label to jumping to the kill_exec_queue label when err is nonzero.
intent_record.how: At runtime, a failure to add the exec queue to the hardware engine group now follows the kill_exec_queue cleanup path instead of the put_exec_queue path, causing more complete teardown of the partially created exec queue and preventing it from being left in an inconsistent or improperly cleaned-up state.

intent_record.intent_summary: Fix the xa_alloc failure cleanup path to remove the exec queue from its hardware engine group before destroying it.
intent_record.what: The error path after a failed xa_alloc() in xe_exec_queue_create_ioctl() was changed from jumping directly to kill_exec_queue to first jumping to a new del_hw_engine_group label, which conditionally calls xe_hw_engine_group_del_exec_queue(q->hwe->hw_engine_group, q) when q->vm, q->hwe, and q->hwe->hw_engine_group are present, and then falls through to the existing cleanup path.
intent_record.how: When exec queue ID allocation fails, the function now removes the newly created exec queue from its hardware engine group before killing the queue, preventing stale group membership and ensuring associated state is cleaned up consistently during this failure path.

grouping_result.intent: Fix the xa_alloc failure cleanup path to remove the exec queue from its hardware engine group before destroying it.

consistency_review.core_intent: Ensure exec queue creation failure paths perform full teardown, including unregistering the queue from its hardware engine group before destruction.

relevance_review.reason: The changes specifically fix exec queue creation error-unwind paths so the exec_queue is fully unregistered from owning lists, including the hardware engine group, before destruction—matching the root cause of freeing the queue while stale list references remained.

candidates.rationale: On hardware engine group registration failure, this jumps to a cleanup path that only drops/destroys the exec_queue instead of performing the full teardown needed to unregister it from owning lists, leaving stale references.

When xa_alloc fails, this directs control to a cleanup sequence that kills the exec_queue without first removing it from the hardware engine group, matching the incorrect unwind ordering that causes dangling list references.
This destruction step is executed in the faulty unwind path before the queue has been removed from all owner lists, directly causing the freed exec_queue to remain referenced and enabling UAF.

vuln_statements.explanation: This statement frees/kills the exec_queue in the error-unwind path before it has been removed from all owning lists, which is the direct cause of the stale-list-reference and dangling-pointer/use-after-free condition described in the root cause.

On xa_alloc failure, this branches into the faulty unwind path that reaches xe_exec_queue_kill(q) without first unregistering the exec_queue from the hw_engine_group and other owners, creating the incorrect teardown ordering.

When hardware engine group registration fails, this sends control to an incomplete cleanup path that does not perform full teardown and list removal before dropping the exec_queue, contributing to the stale-reference bug.

bic_trace_step.reason: The snippet includes the full body of `xe_exec_queue_create_ioctl()` and the related teardown helpers, so it is sufficient to judge the error-unwind behavior. The vulnerable pattern is present in the create ioctl: after creating `q`, user extensions may enable compute mode via `exec_queue_set_compute_mode()`, which calls `xe_vm_add_compute_exec_queue(vm, q)` and links the object into the VM compute list (`err = xe_vm_add_compute_exec_queue(vm, q); ... q->flags |= EXEC_QUEUE_FLAG_COMPUTE_MODE`). Later, `xe_exec_queue_create_ioctl()` can still fail on subsequent steps such as the compute-mode consistency check or `xa_alloc(...)`, and then it unwinds through `put_exec_queue:` with only `xe_exec_queue_kill(q); xe_exec_queue_put(q);`. In `xe_exec_queue_kill()`, compute-list removal happens only through `exec_queue_kill_compute(q)`, but that function starts with `if (!xe_vm_in_compute_mode(q->vm)) return;` and otherwise removes only `list_del(&q->compute.link); --q->vm->preempt.num_exec_queues;`. There is no corresponding removal from any owning hw-engine-group list during this unwind path, and destruction/finalization paths shown (`xe_exec_queue_destroy()` and `xe_exec_queue_fini()`) also do not remove `q` from such owning lists before freeing (`kfree(q)`). Thus the buggy construct described by the root cause remains: an exec_queue can be freed during create-ioctl error unwind without being removed from all owning lists, leaving stale references. No fix is visible here, such as reordered unwind or explicit delisting from both VM compute and hw_engine_group ownership before the final put/free.

bic_trace_step.reason: The diff is sufficient because it shows the relevant create-path error handling inside xe_exec_queue_create_ioctl() and the unwind labels. The root cause is incorrect unwind ordering where an exec_queue could be freed without first being removed from owning lists such as the VM compute exec queue list. In this commit, when compute mode is inherited from the VM, the queue is added to the VM list before extensions are processed: `err = xe_vm_add_compute_exec_queue(vm, q); if (XE_IOCTL_DBG(xe, err)) goto put_exec_queue;`. Crucially, later failures no longer jump directly to `put_exec_queue`; both the extension failure and xa_alloc failure paths now go to `kill_exec_queue`: `if (XE_IOCTL_DBG(xe, err)) goto kill_exec_queue;` and `if (err) goto kill_exec_queue;`. The cleanup ordering is `kill_exec_queue: xe_exec_queue_kill(q);` followed by `put_exec_queue: xe_exec_queue_put(q);`. This indicates the queue is killed/removed from owning structures before the final put/free, which is the correct fix for the stale-list-reference/UAF issue. Therefore the vulnerable construct (free via put without prior removal from lists on these failure paths) is absent in this version, and the fix is present.

bic_trace_step.reason: The diff is sufficient because it shows the relevant create and destroy paths for registration/unwind of exec queues with the hw_engine_group. The root cause is incorrect error-unwind ordering that could free an exec_queue without removing it from owning lists. In this commit, the create path explicitly registers the queue with the hw engine group only after prior setup succeeds: `if (q->vm && q->hwe->hw_engine_group) { err = xe_hw_engine_group_add_exec_queue(q->hwe->hw_engine_group, q); if (err) goto put_exec_queue; }` inside `xe_exec_queue_create_ioctl()`. This means the queue is added through a dedicated helper that can safely manage list linkage, and failure of the add helper causes unwind before successful completion. The allocation path also initializes the list head with `INIT_LIST_HEAD(&q->hw_engine_group_link);`, which is consistent with safe list handling. On destruction, the queue is explicitly removed from the hw engine group before kill/free logic: `if (q->vm && q->hwe->hw_engine_group) xe_hw_engine_group_del_exec_queue(q->hwe->hw_engine_group, q);` followed by `xe_exec_queue_kill(q);`. That removal-before-destruction ordering is the essence of the fix for stale list references. Therefore the vulnerable construct (freeing while still linked in the hw_engine_group list) is not present here, and the function already contains the fix.
